rules.title: Berkeley prohibition on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement:
It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. It is also unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels.

A coordinated pricing algorithm is any analytical or computational process that uses Competitor Data to calculate and recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other rental contract terms for future leases. The coordination is between a Berkeley landlord and one or more competitors, including through a third-party vendor. Competitor Data is nonpublic rent, occupancy, lease-date and similar data on properties the landlord does not own or manage, when the data is less than 90 days old.

Each month a violation continues, and each unit for which the algorithm was used, is a separate violation.

Enforcement:
- The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
- An aggrieved tenant may sue a landlord user for injunctive relief, money damages and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
- A prevailing City Attorney or tenant receives mandatory attorney's fees and costs. Lease clauses limiting a tenant's fees are unenforceable.

The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation; Competitor Data = nonpublic data less than 90 days old; mandatory attorney's fees to a prevailing City Attorney or tenant

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley, to landlords setting their rents or occupancy, and to vendors who sell, license or provide coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords. No unit-count, building-age or owner limits. Operates alongside the state Cartwright Act algorithm ban (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729).
coverage.other_conditions: Excluded products: (a) aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that make no recommendations; (b) products used to set affordable-housing rent or income limits; (c) information used for project-financing market research, appraisals, or software research, testing or training, provided Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated.

rules.exemptions: The definition excludes: aggregated and anonymous rental data reports that do not recommend rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable-housing guidelines; and information used for project-financing market research, appraisals, or software research, testing or training, where Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated.
rules.effective_date_note: The captured ordinance text (D001) states no effective date and no final adoption date. It records only that the ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025; the document URL refers to a December 2, 2025 agenda item. The only published effective date in the documents is the secondary DX06 alert's 'effective January 2026' (month only). Status in_force as of 2026-10-01 is consistent with that date.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance Annual General Adjustment cap (Measure BB 5% maximum; 2026 AGA 1.0%)
rules.requirement:
Landlords of fully covered units may raise the permanent rent ceiling each year only by the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) set by the Rent Board.

Formula and cap:
- The AGA is 65% of the Bay Area CPI-U increase (formula approved by voters in November 2004).
- Measure BB caps the AGA at 5%.
- Landlords with banked (unused) prior AGAs may still exceed 5% to reach the rent ceiling.

The 2026 AGA Order (Rent Board Regulation 1148), adopted October 16, 2025:
- Lets eligible landlords raise 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0%, no earlier than January 1, 2026.
- 1.0% is 65% of the 1.5% CPI increase for July 2024 to June 2025.
- Does not adjust rents for tenancies that began on or after January 1, 2025 with rents set under Costa-Hawkins.
- Regulation 1148 sets the qualifying conditions and the required notice to tenants.

Other Measure BB changes:
- Rent increases may be petitioned only for completed capital improvements.
- In fully covered tenancies starting on or after February 6, 2024, utilities must be in base rent or separately metered in the tenant's name.
- Government-owned or subsidized units registered as fully covered now have AGA-limited rent ceilings.
rules.key_value: 2026 AGA 1.0% of 2025 permanent rent ceilings (65% of 1.5% Bay Area CPI-U, July 2024-June 2025), no earlier than Jan. 1, 2026; AGA capped at 5% (Measure BB); banked AGAs may exceed 5% up to the rent ceiling

unverifiable_exemptions: Single-family home with a tenancy that began on or after January 1, 1996 (partially covered, no rent control)
Most condominiums (partially covered, no rent control)

Section 202 or Section 811 subsidized units, and Rent Supplement, Section 8 Loan Management Set Aside or Project-based Section 8 units in projects with a HUD-insured or HUD-held mortgage (partially covered)
Golden Duplex: owner-occupied on December 31, 1979 and an owner currently lives in one unit
Owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant and lived on the property when the tenancy started
Tenancy started after Nov 7, 2018 on a property where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied
University rental units such as dormitories
Nonprofit cooperative
Tenancy began on or after Jan 1, 2025 with rent set under Costa-Hawkins (not adjusted by the 2026 AGA)
coverage.owner_conditions: Golden Duplex exemption: owner-occupied on Dec 31, 1979 and currently owner-occupied. The shared kitchen/bath exemption applies only if the owner lived on the property when the tenancy started. ADU-property exemption: tenancies started after Nov 7, 2018 where either unit is owner-occupied.
coverage.other_conditions: Single-family homes are fully covered only if the current tenancy began before 1996. Government-subsidized units (Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME and others) are fully or partially covered depending on unit type. The 2026 AGA does not apply to tenancies beginning on or after Jan 1, 2025 with Costa-Hawkins rents.

rules.effective_date_note: The documents give no original effective date for the Rent Ordinance's AGA provisions. The 65% of CPI formula was approved by voters in November 2004. Measure BB (with the 5% cap) passed in November 2024, and D006 states no operative date for the cap. The 2026 AGA Order was adopted Oct 16, 2025 and may be applied no earlier than Jan 1, 2026.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance just cause for eviction, notice requirements and owner move-in relocation assistance
rules.requirement:
Tenants in fully or partially covered units cannot be evicted without just cause.

Measure BB limits on causes:
- Nonpayment eviction is allowed only if rental debt is at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent (Oakland-Fremont metro) for an equivalent unit.
- A tenant may not be evicted for refusing to sign a substantially similar new lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
- A lease-breach eviction requires a mutually agreed material term, substantial actual damage to the landlord, and unreasonable tenant behavior. The prior notice to cease must specify the term and describe the violation and harm.

Notice duties:
- Any termination notice must state that advice is available from the Rent Board and give its housing counseling phone number and website.
- Copies of termination notices, notices to quit and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days of service.
- For tenancies starting on or after Dec 20, 2024, landlords must give a written Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days and post it in any interior common area.

Owner move-in evictions require relocation assistance, which the Rent Board must adjust for inflation each year. From Jan 1, 2026 the amounts are $19,413 standard plus $6,471 for qualifying households.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if debt >= 1 month HUD FMR; termination notices and eviction filings copied to the Rent Board within 3 business days; Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days (tenancies from Dec 20, 2024); owner move-in relocation from Jan 1, 2026: $19,413 standard plus $6,471 for qualifying households (1.5% CPI-U adjustment)

Owner shares a kitchen or bath with the tenant and lived on the property when the tenancy started
Tenancy started after Nov 7, 2018 on a property where one unit is an ADU and either unit is owner-occupied

Qualifying-household criteria for the additional relocation payment are not stated
coverage.summary: Just cause applies to both fully and partially covered units: pre-1980 multifamily units, single-family homes regardless of tenancy start, rooming houses, post-June 1980 new construction, most condominiums, and government-subsidized units. Only the listed exempt unit types are outside it. Covered properties follow this local ordinance instead of state Civ. Code § 1946.2.

coverage.other_conditions: The additional relocation payment applies only to qualifying households.

- university rental units
- nonprofit cooperatives
rules.effective_date_note: The documents give no original effective date for the just-cause provisions. Measure BB passed in November 2024, and its Notice of Tenant Rights duty applies to tenancies started on or after Dec 20, 2024. The 2026 relocation amounts were approved Oct 16, 2025 and take effect Jan 1, 2026.

rules.title: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance relocation assistance
rules.requirement: When tenants are evicted so the owner can remove the property from the rental housing market (Ellis Act), the owner must pay the same relocation assistance as for an owner move-in eviction. Payments are indexed to inflation, and the Rent Board publishes the yearly increase. From January 1, 2026 the standard payment is $19,413, plus an additional $6,471 for qualifying households.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance security deposit interest requirement
rules.requirement: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on the security deposit at the end of each year. If the tenant moves out before year end, the landlord must pay a prorated amount. Deposit caps, the 21-day return deadline and photo rules are state law (Civ. Code § 1950.5), not part of this record.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies (BMC ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement:
An owner or agent who charges an applicant a fee for a consumer credit report and application processing must disclose two things, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee (BMC 13.78.010):
- a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement;
- the maximum fee cap under Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).

An owner may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate's departure or a request to add or replace a roommate (BMC 13.78.016).

The chapter applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease terms, and conflicting lease provisions are unenforceable (BMC 13.78.018).

The dollar cap, receipt, credit-report copy and refund rules are state law (Civ. Code § 1950.6).
rules.key_value: Pre-payment disclosure of the screening fee rights statement and the state fee cap; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants; no Berkeley dollar cap (Rent Board lists the state maximum as $68.96 for 2026)

coverage.summary: Applies to owners of residential rental property in Berkeley and their agents, and to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language. Operates alongside Civ. Code § 1950.6.

rules.effective_date_note: The documents give no effective date for BMC ch. 13.78.
